question:
A 37-year-old man who had undergone liver transplantation 7 years ago, presents to the physician because of yellowish discoloration of the skin, sclera, and urine. He is on regular immunosuppressive therapy and is well-adherent to the treatment. He has no comorbidities and is not taking any other medication. He provides a history of similar episodes of yellowish skin discoloration 6–7 times since he underwent liver transplantation. Physical examination shows clinical jaundice. Laboratory studies show:
While blood cell (WBC) count 4,400/mm3
Hemoglobin 11.1 g/dL
Serum creatinine 0.9 mg/dL
Serum bilirubin (total) 44 mg/dL
Aspartate transaminase (AST) 1,111 U/L
Alanine transaminase (ALT) 671 U/L
Serum gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase 777 U/L
Alkaline phosphatase 888 U/L
Prothrombin time 17 seconds
A Doppler ultrasound shows significantly reduced blood flow into the transplanted liver. A biopsy of the transplanted liver is likely to show which of the following histological features?

options.opa: Normal architecture of bile ducts and hepatocytes
options.opb: Broad fibrous septations with formation of micronodules
options.opd: Irregularly shaped nodules of regenerating hepatocytes with peripheral halo
options.ope: Interstitial cellular infiltration with parenchymal fibrosis, obliterative arteritis

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Liver transplantation -> Immunosuppressive therapy -> Recurrent episodes of yellowish skin discoloration -> Clinical jaundice -> Laboratory findings of elevated bilirubin, AST, ALT, gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, and alkaline phosphatase levels -> Doppler ultrasound showing reduced blood flow into the transplanted liver -> Histological features likely to show broad fibrous septations with formation of micronodules -> 95%
enhanced_information: The histological features of the transplanted liver in this patient with recurrent episodes of yellowish skin discoloration and clinical jaundice are likely to show broad fibrous septations with formation of micronodules, supported by the Doppler ultrasound findings of reduced blood flow into the liver.
analysis: The patient's history of recurrent yellowish skin discoloration and clinical jaundice, along with the significantly reduced blood flow into the transplanted liver on Doppler ultrasound, suggests a chronic process affecting the liver. The enhanced information supports the histological features of broad fibrous septations with formation of micronodules. This pattern is consistent with chronic rejection in a transplanted liver, leading to biliary fibrosis and nodular regeneration. Ballooning degeneration of hepatocytes is more characteristic of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, irregularly shaped nodules of regenerating hepatocytes with peripheral halo are seen in focal nodular hyperplasia, and interstitial cellular infiltration with parenchymal fibrosis, obliterative arteritis are features of chronic rejection in other solid organ transplants, not specifically liver transplants.
